behavior: An empty `id` counts as no `id`, as a prop or as an attribute of a part. The part then has the id that it has with no `id`, and each part that names it names that id. Base UI keeps an empty `id` in most parts. HTML requires a nonempty id with no ASCII white space, and no ID reference can name the resulting `id=""`. A dialog, a popover, a menu, a group, a fieldset, a meter, a progress bar, a tab panel or a toast then has no name. A field, a dialog, a popover or a toast loses its description, and a label names no control. Two selects, comboboxes or date fields with `id=""` give the same derived ids, and the second one takes the name of the first. Base UI's `Collapsible.Panel`, `Accordion.Trigger` and `Checkbox.Root` already treat an empty `id` as no `id`. Base UI keeps an `id` of white space only even in those three parts, while Vase UI treats it as absent because ASCII white space separates ids in an ID reference list.
